 AFA confirms semi-automated offside to debut in Argentina on 12 December 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article The federation announced the semi-automated offside system will launch in Argentina on 12 December at Estadio Único de La Plata, venue for the Torneo Clausura final.
 The decision followed an AFA meeting of senior officials, which also set the new 2027 Primera División format.
 OneFootball Videos
 Argentinos Juniors president Cristian Malaspina hailed the upgrade and said the provider had tabled very positive proposals. He said that, given implementation timings, the system will be in every top-flight stadium from the second half of next year.
 Although in June the AFA had pencilled in general use for 2027, work has accelerated. Officials are seeking to introduce the system early in the Copa Argentina final, where Platense await the winner of Boca v Banfield, and in the Recopa de Campeones in January 2027.
 Technically, the system deploys a dozen tactical tracking cameras dedicated to capturing the ball’s exact position. It also logs up to 29 specific data points per player, focusing on limbs that determine offside calls.
 The official ball carries an internal sensor that transmits the instant of contact. That data is cross-checked in real time by artificial intelligence to detect offside autonomously, sending an alert to the video booth so VAR can validate decisions faster and reduce human error.
 The technology already operates in elite competitions, including the UEFA Champions League since 2022/2023 and the last two FIFA World Cups. Its rollout in Argentina marks a significant step towards modern, transparent reviews of complex incidents.
